setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The Scale editor is open on slot 1, C major, which is the applied scale and is lit brightly on grid row 3. Slots 2 and 3 keep their default settings and are not applied. The sequencer is stopped.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Hold K1 and tap slot 2 at (2,3). The title row names slot 2 and its button lights dimly, while slot 1 stays bright: slot 2 is selected for editing but is not applied.
steps.title: Select slot 2 for editing

steps.caption: Turn E2 to Root, turn E3 two detents up to D and press K3 to save. Slot 2 now holds D major, but it is still not applied.
steps.title: Save D as the root

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), then Stop. The phrase still plays C, D, E, F, because slot 1 is the applied scale and slot 2 is only being edited.
steps.title: Hear that nothing changed

steps.caption: Tap slot 2 at (2,3). Its button lights brightly: it is now the applied scale.
steps.title: Apply slot 2

steps.caption: Tap Play, then Stop. The phrase plays D major: D, E, F#, G (MIDI 62, 64, 66, 67), with the same rhythm and velocities.
steps.title: Hear D major

title: Save D major, then apply it
